parts.solution_md:
Expand the bracket

$5x-5=3x+7$

**[M1]**

Subtract $3x$from both sides

$2x-5=7$

Add 5 to both sides

$2x=12$

**[M1]**

Divide by 2 on both sides

$x=6$

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **M1**: For expanding the bracket.
> 
> **M1**: For correct method to isolate the $x$ term. This can be shown by $5x-3x=7+5$.
> 
> **A1**: Correct answer.

parts.problem_md:
Esme buys 8 magazines at \$2.45 each and y cards at \$3.15 each.
Esme spends \$60.55 in total.

How many cards does she buy?
parts.solution_md:
> *One magazine costs \$2.45. Find the cost of 8 magazines.*

$8 \times \$ 2.45 = \$ 19.60$

> *Esme spent \$60.55 in total so subtract the cost of the magazines to find out how much she spent on cards.*

$\$ 60.55 - \$ 19.60 = \$ 40.95$

**[1]**

> *To work out how many cards she bought, divide the total cost of the cards by the cost of one card.*

$\$ 40.95 \div \$ 3.15 = 13$

**13**** ****[1]**

parts.problem_md:
Rovers, United and City are football teams.

Rovers scored$x$goals. 
United scored 8 goals more than Rovers. 
City scored 3 goals less than twice the number of goals scored by Rovers.

The three teams scored a total of 117 goals.

Write down and solve an equation to find the value of $x$.

$x$ = .................................................
parts.solution_md:
> *Write the number of goals for each team using algebra.*

* **Rovers = *$x$

*United = *$x+8$

*City = *$2x-3$

* ***[1]**

> *Add the expressions and equate to 117 (the three teams scored a total of 117 goals). *

$x+x+8+2x-3=117$

**[1]**

> *Combine like terms.*

> * *$4x+5=117$

**[1]**

> *Subtract 5 from both sides.*

> * *$4x=117-5\,\,4x=112$

> *Divide both sides by 4.*

> * *$x=112\div4$

$x=28$* ***[1]**

**working must be shown, answer alone only gains one mark**

equations.alt: x plus x plus 8 plus 2 x minus 3 equals 117
bold italic x bold equals bold 28

parts.problem_md:
In this part, all measurements are in centimetres.

![qp7f-0580-33-paper-3-nov-2020-cie-igcse-maths](assets/001-qp7f-0580-33-paper-3-nov-2020-cie-igcse-maths.png)

The diagram shows a kite with sides $( 2 x + 5 )$ and $( 3 x - 1 )$. The perimeter of the kite is 33 cm.

Work out the length of a shorter side.

............................................ cm
parts.solution_md:
> *Work out the perimeter of the kite by adding all the sides.*

> * *$( 3 x - 1 ) + ( 3 x - 1 ) + ( 2 x + 5 ) + ( 2 x + 5 )$

* ***[1]**

> *Rearrange to write all the *$x$* terms together and combine like terms. *

$3x+3x+2x+2x-1-1+5+5=10x+8$

> *Set equal to 33.*

$10x+8=33$

> * [1]*

> *Subtract 8 from both sides.*

> * *$10x=33-8\,\,10x=25$

* ***[1]**

> *Divide both sides by 10 to solve for *$x$*.*

> * *$x=25\div10\,\,x=2.5$

**[1]**

> *Substitute *$x=2.5$* into *$3x-1$* (the length of the shorter side).*

> * *$( 3 \times 2.5 ) - 1 = 6.5$

> * *

**6.5 cm** **[1]**

equations.alt: 3 x plus 3 x plus 2 x plus 2 x minus 1 minus 1 plus 5 plus 5 equals 10 x plus 8

x equals 25 divided by 10

x equals 2.5

parts.problem_md:
A club is arranging transport for its members.

Speedy Coaches charge \$625 plus \$15 per member.

The total cost, in dollars, for x members is given by the expression $15x+625.$

i) Sporty Coaches charge \$117 plus \$19 per member.

Write an expression for the total cost, in dollars, for $x$members.

[2]

ii) The total cost is the same for both Speedy Coaches and Sporty Coaches.

Write down an equation and solve it to find $x$.

$x$= .............................................. [3]
parts.solution_md:
i) *Using the same linear format as given for Speedy Coaches and as the rate is *`$ 19`* per member, the cost for *$x$* members is multiplied by *$19$

$19x+f$

**[1]**

> *where *$f$* is the fixed price*

> *As the fixed price *`f equals $ 117`*, the expression for the total cost for Sporty Coaches is*

$19x+117$ **[1]**

** **

ii) *As the total cost is the same, form an equation where the expression for Speedy Coaches is equal to the expression for Sporty Coaches*

$15x+625=19x+117$

**[1]**

> *Solve this equation for *$x$

$\begin{gathered} 15 x + 625 - 117 & = 19 x \\ 15 x + 508 & = 19 x \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

$\begin{gathered} 508 = 19 x - 15 x \\ 508 = 4 x \\ x = 508 \div 4 \end{gathered}$

$x=127$ **[1]**

equations.alt: bold 19 bold italic x bold plus bold 117
bold italic x bold equals bold 127

parts.problem_md:
Cara has $n$ pencils. 
Alice has twice as many pencils as Cara. 
Leon has three more pencils than **Alice**. 
The three children have a total of 58 pencils.

Use this information to write down an equation and solve it to find the value of $n$.

$n$ = ...................................................
parts.solution_md:
> *First find an expression for how many pencils each person has.*

*Cara = ***n**

*Alice = 2***n**

*Leon = 2***n*** + 3*

**2n or 2n + 3 ****[1]**

> *Form an equation, given that the total is 58*

$n+2n+2n+3=58$

**[1]**

> *Simplify by collecting like terms*

$5n+3=58$

> *Solve for **n** by subtracting 3 from both sides*

$5n=55$

**[1]**

> *Divide both sides by 5*

$n=11$

**n ****= 11**** ****[1]**

5 n space plus thin space 3 space equals space 58

parts.problem_md:
In this part, all angles are in degrees.

![qp7d-0580-33-paper-3-may-2020-cie-igcse-maths](assets/002-qp7d-0580-33-paper-3-may-2020-cie-igcse-maths.png)

i) Use the information in the triangle to write down an equation in terms of $x$.

[1]

ii) Solve this equation to find the value of $x.$

$x$= ................................................. [3]

iii) Work out the size of the smallest angle in the triangle.

[2]
parts.solution_md:
(i) *Add all the angles together and put equal to 180 (angles in a triangle add up to *$180^{\circ}$*).*

> * *$2x+x+23+2x-13=180$

* *$2x+x+23+2x-13=180$* ***[1]**

(ii) *Rearrange the terms to get the *$x$* terms together, then combine like terms.*

> * *$\begin{gathered} 2 x + x + 2 x + 23 - 13 & = 180 \\ \\ 5 x + 10 & = 180 \end{gathered}$

*   ***[1] **

> *Subtract 10 from both sides.*

$5x=180-10\,\,5x=170$

> * Divide both sides by 5.*

> * *$x=170\div5$

**[1]   **

$x=34^{\circ}$* ***[1]**

(iii) *Substitute *$x=34$* into each of the expressions for the angles in the triangle. *

$\begin{gathered} 2 \times 34 & = 68 \\ \\ 34 + 23 & = 57 \\ \\ 2 \times 34 - 13 & = 55 \end{gathered}$

* ***[1]**

> *The smallest one is 55.*

* *$55^{\circ}$* ***[1]**

i) Navja weighs a parcel with mass $w$kg on her scales. She uses the masses shown to balance the scales.

![qp1bi-0580-32-paper-3-march-2020-cie-igcse-maths](assets/003-qp1bi-0580-32-paper-3-march-2020-cie-igcse-maths.png)

Work out the value of $w$.

$w$ = ................................................. [3]

ii) Sometimes Navja uses an electronic weighing machine. The machine gives the mass, $p$ kg, of a parcel as 12.4kg, correct to the nearest 100g.

Complete this statement about the value of $p$.

.................. `less-than or slanted equal to p less than` ................... [2]
parts.solution_md:
i) *Convert all masses to kilograms*

* **5 g = 0.005 kg*

*10 g = 0.01 kg*

*20 g, 0.02 kg*

**[1]**

> *Form an equation from the balanced scales*

$\begin{gathered} 0.005 + 0.01 + 0.02 + w & = 2 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

$\begin{gathered} 0.035 + w & = 2 \end{gathered}$

> *Solve the equation for *$w$

> * *$w=2-0.035$

**1.965 kg*** ***[1]**

** **

ii) *Convert the mass of the parcel into grams by multiplying by *$1000$

* **12.4 kg = 12400 g*

> *The error interval has a range of *$100g$*, halve this*

$100\div2=50$

> *In two separate calculations, add and subtract *$50g$* to determine the limits of the error interval*

*Lower limit: *$12400-50=12350$

*Upper limit: *$12400+50=12450$

> *Convert values back to kilograms by dividing by 1000 and place into the error interval *

*12350 g = 12.35 kg*

*12450 g = 12.45 kg*

** ****12.35**$\leqp<$**12.45** **[2]**

**1 mark for each correct value in kg**
